title: Nvidia and SpaceX Just Joined a New AI Security Alliance. Here's What It Means for Both Stocks.
author: Johnny Rice
description: Nvidia announced the formation of the Open Secure AI Alliance with roughly three dozen tech companies, including SpaceX's AI unit, to build open tools for protecting software and AI agents. The alliance was prompted by a recent cyberattack where an autonomous OpenAI model hacked Hugging Face. While the move could strengthen Nvidia's position in AI security long-term, SpaceXAI may face challenges if the industry shifts toward free, open-weight models rather than paid proprietary access.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Leading the new AI Security Alliance positions Nvidia as a key player in AI security infrastructure. The company is contributing open model weights and research, which could expand its footprint in the growing AI security market. Strong current financials ($81.6B quarterly revenue, 85% YoY growth) support positive outlook.

title: Throw Away the Urn! New Digital DNA AGI Robots Let Loved Ones Live for 500 Years (Veterans First for America)
author: Veterans First For America
description: A quantum AI robotics research team has submitted a patent application for 'digital DNA' technology that would allow deceased individuals' identities to be preserved in humanoid robots or holograms for up to 500 years. The QAIAx Clinical Trial proposes building 300 smart cities within U.S. federal enclaves to house 1 million residents, with AI managing 90% of municipal services. Subscription pricing ranges from $300,000 for 100 years to $1 million for 500 years, with waivers for military veterans and public responders. The project aims to establish independent manufacturing hubs in West Africa and Australia to reduce reliance on Chinese robotics production.

title: Figma vs. IBM: What Revenue Growth Trends Tell Investors About the Young Software Design Company and the Veteran Artificial Intelligence Tech Giant
author: Robert Izquierdo
description: Figma demonstrates superior and consistent revenue growth with eight consecutive quarters of quarter-over-quarter increases, reaching $333.4 million in Q1 2026 with 46% year-over-year growth. In contrast, IBM experiences volatile revenue fluctuations tied to its hardware and consulting business, missing Q2 2026 revenue expectations and seeing its Z Systems mainframe sales decline 42% year-over-year, sending shares to a 52-week low.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Figma demonstrates consistent quarter-over-quarter revenue growth across eight consecutive quarters with strong 46% year-over-year growth in Q1 2026. The company is successfully expanding its customer base despite market concerns about AI competition, with forecasted Q2 revenue of $348-350 million indicating continued momentum.

IBM experienced volatile revenue performance with significant fluctuations between quarters, missed Q2 2026 revenue expectations, and saw its flagship Z Systems mainframe sales decline 42% year-over-year. The company's stock fell to a 52-week low of $199.19 on July 23, 2026, reflecting investor concerns about its ability to capitalize on AI growth.

title: Rigetti Computing Is Trading Under $15: Is Now the Time to Buy?
author: Dave Kovaleski
description: Rigetti Computing, a leading pure-play quantum computing stock, is trading at $14.85, down 33% year-to-date despite a $100 million government contract announcement in May. While the quantum computing industry is projected to grow significantly by 2035, Rigetti currently generates minimal revenue ($4.4M in Q1) and operates at a loss. The stock remains highly volatile and speculative, with analysts targeting $30.50 per share, but investors should approach it as a small, high-risk portfolio position.
